answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require a costly voyage of verifiable service before any identity earns paid work. Each newcomer starts at zero and must finish small, checkable tasks whose receipts are bound to that identity and time window. That history is the trust signal others rely on: only agents with a sustained record cross the horizon into better jobs. An attacker spawning thousands of fakes must pay compute and time per identity, yet each fake still starts at zero and cannot transfer reputation, so flooding yields no paid work and costs more than it earns.
